x: In the senior event we were short of our best performers but it was good to see Archie Bedford once more in our midst and even more refreshing to see him running well enough to be our first man home in fourth place.
Archie Bedford returned for one of his rare visits and, by finishing fifth, proved he still has the capacity to gain a place in our first teams.

A spectacular return to form by Charlie Dabbs, a defiant battle against "father time" and injuries successfully overcome by Archie Bedford, and an extraordinary run by Clive Shippen were just a few of the highlights to emerge from this event, considered by some to be an unofficial "Brighton" trial.
He was relieved on the tricky Dale Hill stage by "veteran" Archie Bedford who put us well clear of the rest of the field. The last man, but by no means the least, was John Moore.

Shippen moved through well over the last mile and he was closely followed by Archie Bedford who had run steadily throughout. Bob Glover found out too late that one mustn't underestimate the finishing speed of those behind, especially when they include an accomplished half miler like Gerald Batty of Rochester!
Walker were well to the fore early on, and with Colin Collis, Archie Bedford, Len Bishop and Bob Plummer quite well placed, it seemed as if we might gain a team place in this well contested race.
Colin Collis, making a very successful comeback, was our first man home. He was closely followed by Eric Gebbett and Archie Bedford who both ran well in very difficult conditions.

Unfortunately, for a variety of reasons, Archie Bedford, John Davies, Colin Collis and Clive Shippen were unable to run, so with six to score and a "12 cup" in the offing we were able to start nine only.
Archie Bedford continued for the 'A' and did 24.30 to retain 10th position. Eddie Short, running for the 'C' remained in 13th place but Dennis Jones dropped the 'D' back to 14th.
Archie Bedford, although on the wrong side of forty, put up a plucky effort across Gatwick Aerodrome and, despite being forced to give way to Shaftesbury, can be said to have run true to form.

Meanwhile John Moore and Archie Bedford were battling it out shoulder to shoulder and remained that way til the last half-mile, when John, who had almost been dropped a couple of minutes earlier, drew away to take 3rd. place.

Going off down Copse Hill the three leaders were still locked together but the field behind had started to string out, although it was noticed that John Moore, Jim Radford and Archie Bedford who had started slowly were working their way through.
The Editors have been taken to task for withholding vital information re our increased membership. Both Archie Bedford and Eddie Short claim they were daddies before the issue of our last gazette.

Pat Newell ran very well in his first race for many months to gain second place and Barry Sawyer, despite not being in full training, took the bronze. That promising fledgling Archie Bedford, still only 44 years old, turned in a brisk 32:51 to get amongst the standard medals once more.
Names to disappear are:- Dave Baulch, Charlie Smart, Barry Sawyer, John Dear, Mal Robinson, Pete Bagnall, John Bromley, Ray Tooby, Archie Bedford and Kelly Diprose.

Archie Bedford was our next runner and he returned a time of 14:26 which beat the old record of 14:30 and then Bill Lucas took over for the final leg and he did 14:11 which was only beaten by Chataway of Walton, who put up a new record time of 14:02 for this course of 2.94 miles.
